purpose: Qualify version-2 monotonic marker measurement with bounded browser clock alignment under capacity and delay/jitter/loss changes
interpretation: All four cases have valid marker measurements, including every collected phase. Maximum browser alignment uncertainty is 1.298 to 1.423 ms, inside the unchanged 5 ms limit. No rejected, omitted, malformed or reversed markers occur.

Three cases pass all unchanged gates: direct delay/jitter/loss, adaptive MediaMTX source delay/jitter/loss, and direct 4 Mbit/s capacity. The fourth fails playback only: a 193 ms freeze during source-capacity recovery. Its latency measurement remains valid; a valid instrument does not establish successful delivery.

The delay/jitter/loss cases use 60 ms one-way delay, 15 ms jitter and 1% random loss. Neither has a freeze or dropped decoded frame. Baseline/impaired median marker-to-expected-composition latency is 45.197/108.976 ms direct and 48.275/130.343 ms with the custom adapter. These are individual synthetic same-host observations, not hardware-independent guarantees or a path ranking.

Direct capacity has 1.007 s of initial-transition freezes, then no steady constrained or recovery freeze and no dropped decoded frame. Source capacity has 1.495 s initial-transition freezes plus six dropped decoded frames (1.695 s disruption), then the separate 193 ms recovery failure. All four restore the 8 Mbit/s encoder target.

Three trials reach 7.0 to 8.6 ms of wall/performance-clock difference while monotonic calibration stays valid. This diagnostic is no longer used to measure latency. Earlier UTC-marker failures retain their original invalid verdicts; no retrospective offset correction is applied.

The source-capacity recovery frame arrives 194 ms after the preceding frame, with a 33.3 ms RTP timestamp advance and 1.3 ms decoder processing. Its measured pre-encoding-to-composition delay is 187.744 ms. No new loss/NACK/drop accompanies it. See the retained diagnostic; encoding, transport, adapter and host scheduling causation remains unresolved.

No acceptance gate or production transport, buffering, source-quality or encoder policy changes between cases. This fixed 720p30 series uses 2–8 Mbit/s adaptation, FEC 5/1 and 20/30/30/45-second phases; it does not qualify the optional format ladder.

Whole-run CPU/memory includes the qualification probe. It does not isolate probe, format-switch or recording overhead, and the distribution performanceEnvironment gate checks transport-buffer warnings rather than per-phase host scheduling.
